html:
The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) was founded in 1887 to raise money for the gold mines of the Witwatersrand. It is now the largest stock exchange in Africa.

The Witwatersrand gold rush began in 1886, and Johannesburg grew out of a mining camp almost overnight. Deep gold reefs needed costly machinery, so mining companies sold shares to investors in South Africa and London. The exchange gave them a place to trade. Big mining houses such as De Beers and later Anglo American came to dominate it.

For most of the 20th century the JSE was a market for mining and the white economy. Under apartheid foreign sanctions and disinvestment cut it off from much of the world. After 1994 it opened up, moved to electronic trading, and in 2000 left the city centre for Sandton. Today it lists hundreds of companies, and some of South Africa's biggest firms are also traded in London.
sum: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) was founded in 1887 to raise money for the gold mines of the Witwatersrand. It is now the largest stock exchange in Africa.
